title: TWCX-: a short battery-impedance measurement plan, not a new selector
summary: TWCX- applies TransientWaveCompiler's identifiability and perturbation-selection question to battery electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. It packages a time-cost model, nested leave-one-cell-out selection, a user-facing planner and a fairer set of published/fixed/ARD baselines. The practical signal is that informative mid-frequency measurements can track reference-relative capacity fade cheaply on seven specific coin cells, not that its greedy selector is new or superior to established alternatives.

nodes.claim: A cost-aware electrochemical impedance spectroscopy frequency planner to estimate capacity fade relative to each battery's commissioning reference, evaluated with nested held-out cells and an explicit estimated measurement-time budget.
nodes.survived: On seven Zhang et al. LR2032 cells, the nested leave-one-cell-out 2-second-budget greedy plan used an estimated 0.87 s and obtained 2.65 percentage-point SOH MAE. A 0.5-second-budget plan used 0.34 s and obtained 3.05 pp. The published fixed 17.8 Hz single point reached 3.03 pp in 0.37 s; the published 17.8+2.16 Hz pair reached 3.46 pp, and an ARD-kernel full 60-frequency sweep reached 3.52 pp at an estimated 731 s. The repository provides a CLI, reproducible protocol and browser workbench.
nodes.killed: The 0.5-second planner offered no advantage over the published single 17.8 Hz point; the 2-second greedy choice essentially tied an established ARD ranking (2.65 versus 2.64 pp). The original full-spectrum 4.14 pp result used a weaker kernel, corrected by an ARD 3.52 pp control. This is seven cells, one chemistry and one laboratory; time costs are modeled, not measured; it tracks relative fade, not absolute new-cell grading. It does not reuse the TransientWaveCompiler wave compiler or establish a novel selection algorithm.

edges.why: TWCX- explicitly identifies itself as a practical residue of TransientWaveCompiler's measurement-identifiability question: choose observations that resolve uncertainty. This is inheritance of the measurement-design question, not of its reciprocal wave solver.

motifs.title: A useful measurement is one that earns its cost against simple alternatives
motifs.description: TransientWaveCompiler exposes when passive response data cannot determine a physical realization. TWCX- translates measurement selection into a bounded EIS test-time budget, but strong fixed-frequency and ARD baselines remove the novelty claim for greedy selection. WhatToLookAt and AnotherOddThing pursue related observation-budget questions in different experimental substrates; no shared solver or hardware is implied.
